title: AI BI Reporting and Data Storytelling

questions.question: What is the main risk of AI-written reporting narratives?
options: They can overstate ambiguous metrics, misleading charts, or weak causality
They always include too many metric definitions
questions.explanation: AI reporting narratives need evidence and interpretation controls.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Causality claims need careful review before being written into reporting narratives.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked reporting narrative review plan with controls
questions.explanation: The artifact maps reporting risks to review controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Metric definitions make AI-written data stories reviewable.

questions.question: When should a reporting narrative require review?
options: When decision impact is high or metrics, charts, causality, or audience context are risky
Only when nobody will use the report
Only when all metrics are obvious

questions.question: What should be clear before sharing AI-generated BI text?
options: Metric definition, chart check, causality warning, and decision context
questions.explanation: These controls prevent misleading reporting narratives.
